messages:
sam: Heads up — Acme corp sent a formal request to force traffic for their prod org to the eu-west cluster regardless of client region. They want an exception for latency-sensitive pipelines.

dave: Do we have precedent for per-tenant hard routing? we usually route by geo header + cost policy.

olivia_pm: Sales passed it along. They need an SLA-backed fix, not just a heuristic. They said regulatory reasons could require EU-only pathing.

sam: Right. Proposed quick hack: add a per-tenant routing override that matches X-Redwood-Org header and pins route to a specific pool. Example config: 
```
match: header("X-Redwood-Org") == "acme-prod"
action: route_to(pool: "eu-west-prod-pinned")
```

carla_sre: Danger: headers can be spoofed unless we authenticate the call with org tokens. If we rely only on header matching we open a backdoor.

sam: Agreed. We plan to only accept overrides when request is signed by org key (org token in Authorization) or coming from dedicated customer IP ranges.

dave: Implementation notes: runtime routing table already supports key-based overrides but it's global. We'll need a scoped allowlist and an admin flag in config to opt-in per org. Also need audit logs for any forced route.

olivia_pm: UX ask: console should show "Routing overrides" under org settings with 1) target pool, 2) reason, 3) start/end, 4) forced routes count + last used timestamp. Sales wants a checkbox + approval flow.

raj_sales: Can the console send a webhook to legal to auto-start approval? would speed enterprise on-boarding.

carla_sre: Telemetry: emit a metric like redwood.routing.override.{org_id}.count and span tag override=true so traces show fallback. Also a security event when an override is used from non-expected ip.

sam: Quota question: if a tenant is pinned to eu-west pool, do we still apply org-level quotas and burst limits? we can't let it bypass cost controls.

dave: Quotas remain enforced at ingress; pinned route is a routing preference only. But we need quota visibility per-pool and per-org to avoid noisy neighbors. We'll add quota labels when an override is active.

infra-bot: deploybot: rolling deploy queued for service=route-manager, version=v2.14.9 — ETA 8m.

sam: Timing: if route-manager patch lands, can we ship a soft opt-in (pilot) for Acme? they want it next week.

dave: I can cut a pilot branch that requires admin approval + org token. Will add audit and telemetry. Notary: we'll gate it behind a feature flag.

olivia_pm: I'll wire the console approval flow with a manual step for legal sign-off and attach the approval metadata (signed_by, ticket_id).

carla_sre: One more ask: add an assertion on service-to-service calls so internal requests that originate from other Redwood services respect the override. Without that, some paths will still go to default pool.

sam: Good call. Ok next steps: dave prototype + infra deploy, olivia wire console + approval webhook, carla add telemetry + security events, raj keep Acme informed. I'll draft an internal change notice for customers impacted by routing pinning.

raj_sales: I'll loop Acme in and ask for their org token and IP allowlist.

sam: thanks team :thumbsup:

dave: any objections to using header X-Redwood-Org for matching if we validate it against the org token? otherwise we should use a signed claim.

carla_sre: Prefer a signed jwk claim in the Authorization bearer token (org_id). header-only is last resort.

sam: we'll spec signed claim. I'll push a doc to the eng-platform shared drive with the policy and sample flow.

olivia_pm: thx — please add UI mock for the approval flow, I want to run it by legal tomorrow.

sam: created: https://internal.redwood/notes/1794527890-routing-exception-draft (link)
